parts.title: A night in a lighthouse
parts.instructions: Read the article and choose the best answer for each question.
parts.passage:
When my sister suggested spending a weekend in a lighthouse, I thought she was joking. But the old lighthouse on the north coast really is a hotel now, with four bedrooms and a tiny kitchen at the bottom of the tower.

We arrived on Friday afternoon in heavy rain. The owner, a cheerful man called Mr Baird, showed us to our rooms. Mine was at the top, and to reach it I had to climb a hundred and twenty steps. By the time I arrived, I was out of breath, but the view of the sea through the round window was wonderful.

That evening, we cooked pasta and played cards while the wind shook the walls. I expected to sleep badly, yet I fell asleep quickly and woke up at six, when the sun came through the window and turned the room orange.

The next morning, Mr Baird told us how the lighthouse used to guide ships. Sailors depended on it for two hundred years, until a new machine took over in 1998. I asked him if he missed the old days. 'Sometimes,' he said, 'but it is good to share the place with visitors.' We are going back in October.

questions.prompt: What did the writer think when her sister made the suggestion?
questions.explanation: She thought her sister was joking.

questions.prompt: What was difficult about the writer's room?
questions.explanation: She had to climb a hundred and twenty steps and arrived out of breath.

questions.prompt: How did the writer sleep?
options: She slept until late in the morning
She could not sleep at all
questions.explanation: She expected to sleep badly, yet she fell asleep quickly.

questions.prompt: What did Mr Baird explain?
questions.explanation: He told them how the lighthouse used to guide ships.

questions.prompt: How does Mr Baird feel about the lighthouse now?
options: Sad that it is no longer used
Tired of the work it needs
questions.explanation: He sometimes misses the old days, but it is good to share the place with visitors.

parts.title: My first time in a hostel
parts.instructions: Choose the sentence that fits each gap. There are three extra sentences.
parts.passage:
Last summer, I travelled around Portugal with my cousin, and we decided to stay in hostels to save money. [1] I had always imagined that they were dirty and noisy, but I could not have been more wrong.

Our first hostel was in Porto, in a lovely old house with a roof terrace. [2] There were six beds in our room, and we shared the bathroom with three other people. At first, I felt shy, but the other guests were friendly. [3] One evening, a group from Brazil invited us to a cooking night, and we made a huge dish of rice and beans.

Another good thing was the price. We paid only fifteen euros each per night, which left more money for visiting museums and buying food. [4] We even got a free map and advice on where to go.

Of course, hostels are not perfect. [5] If you are a light sleeper, it is a good idea to bring earplugs. Despite this, I would happily stay in one again.
sentences: We soon began to talk to them every evening.
The room was simple, but it was clean and bright.
The main problem is that someone is always snoring.
It was my first time in a hostel.
She said that we should visit the south first.
The weather in Portugal was hot and sunny every day.
The streets around it were narrow and full of tourists.
The staff at reception were helpful too.

gaps.explanation: "It was my first time" explains why she had only imagined what hostels were like.
"There were six beds in our room" continues the description of the room.
"Them" means the other guests, who were friendly; the next sentence gives an example.
"Helpful too" adds another good point, and the map and advice are examples of help.
"Someone is always snoring" explains why the next sentence mentions earplugs.

parts.title: Welcome to Sunny Hostel
parts.instructions: Write one word in each gap.
parts.passage: Welcome to Sunny Hostel! Breakfast is served [1] 7.30 and 9.30 every morning. Please be quiet [2] eleven o'clock at night, because some guests go to bed early. If you [3] a towel, you can rent one at reception. There is a kitchen [4] you can cook your own meals. [5] you leave, please check that you have taken all your things. We hope [6] will have a lovely stay.

gaps.explanation: A time from one point to another is shown with "between ... and".
Quiet time begins at eleven, so "after" or "from" fits.
The guest asks for a towel, so "need" or "want" fits.
"Where" introduces the place in which guests can cook.
The check happens before or when guests leave.
The hostel hopes that "you" (the guests) will have a nice stay.

parts.title: Welcome to the youth hostel
parts.instructions: Listen to the talk and complete each note. Write one or two words, a number, a date or a time.

turns.speaker: leopold
turns.text: Hello, everyone, and welcome to Riverside Youth Hostel. My name is Leopold, and I’m the manager. Reception is open from seven in the morning until midnight. Some hostels lock the doors at ten, but we don’t. If you come back after midnight, ring the bell, and the night guard will let you in. Now, food. Breakfast is served from seven thirty to nine thirty. It used to cost five pounds, but we have lowered the price, so it’s four pounds now, and it includes as much tea and coffee as you like. The kitchen is open all day if you want to cook for yourself. Next, the laundry. The machines are on the first floor, at the end of the corridor, not in the basement as the old sign says. A wash costs two pounds, but you must bring your own powder. This evening we have a film night. It’s usually at eight, but we start later tonight, at nine, because many people arrive late on Fridays. It’s a comedy, and the popcorn is free. Tomorrow morning there’s a city walk. It’s free, and our guide, Paula, knows lots of stories. We meet at the front door at ten, not at the back door near the bikes, because the bus to the old town stops outside the front. Wear comfortable shoes. Finally, a rule. We have quiet time every night. It starts at eleven, not at ten as in some hostels. After that, please speak softly in the corridors, and don’t use the kitchen. Use the common room if you want to talk. That’s all. Please ask me if you have any questions, and enjoy your stay.

gaps.prompt: Guests who come back after ___ must ring the bell
gaps.explanation: Reception is open until midnight; some hostels lock the doors at ten, but not this one.
It used to be five, but the price is lower now, four pounds.

gaps.prompt: The washing machines are on the ___ floor
gaps.explanation: The old sign says basement, but the machines are on the first floor.

gaps.prompt: Tonight the film begins at ___ o'clock
gaps.explanation: The film is usually at eight but tonight they start later, at nine.

gaps.prompt: For the city walk, meet at the ___ door
gaps.explanation: They meet at the front door, not the back door, because the bus stops outside the front.

gaps.prompt: After ___ o'clock at night, people should speak softly
gaps.explanation: Quiet time starts at eleven, not at ten as in some hostels.

parts.title: A hotel manager
parts.instructions: Listen to the interview and choose the correct answer.

turns.speaker: brigid
turns.text: Ansel, you manage the Seaview Hotel. How did you start working there?

turns.speaker: ansel
turns.text: Many people think I began as a cook because I love food, and I did apply to the kitchen, but it was full. They offered me a job as a cleaner, just for the summer, and I said yes. I wasn’t a receptionist. I was too shy to talk to guests then. That was twenty years ago.

turns.speaker: brigid
turns.text: Any difficult guests?

turns.speaker: ansel
turns.text: Plenty. One man left on the second night. Not because the bed was hard, he said it was the best bed he’d ever had, and the food was fine too. He couldn’t stand the noise of the sea. He said the waves kept him awake. In a hotel on the beach! I couldn’t help laughing, but he was serious.

turns.speaker: brigid
turns.text: What do you do first each day?

turns.speaker: ansel
turns.text: I walk to the breakfast room before anyone gets up and look at everything: the tables, the coffee machine, the flowers. I read my emails later, with a coffee, and I only talk to guests when I’m sure everything is perfect. Breakfast is where people form their first opinion.

turns.speaker: brigid
turns.text: What do you enjoy most about it?

turns.speaker: ansel
turns.text: The hours aren’t short. I work ten hours a day, and I don’t have a free room, my flat is very small. But the people are what I love, from every corner of the world. I’ve learned phrases in fifteen languages, mostly "thank you".

turns.speaker: brigid
turns.text: Have guests ever left strange things behind?

turns.speaker: ansel
turns.text: All the time. Cameras, of course, and one lady left her passport, but she remembered before she left town. The strangest was a violin in a wardrobe. It was a beautiful old one, and nobody knew whose it was. We phoned fifty guests. In the end, a famous musician called us.

turns.speaker: brigid
turns.text: What are your plans for the future?

turns.speaker: ansel
turns.text: Retire? No, not yet. My wife wants me to, but I enjoy it too much. The hotel won’t close either, we painted it last winter. What’s coming is a new hotel in the town of Port Mary, which we are going to open in October, when the leaves change colour. I’ll be very busy.

turns.speaker: brigid
turns.text: Thank you, Ansel. Do you have any message for future guests?

turns.speaker: ansel
turns.text: Just come with an open mind. Tell us what you like, and we will do everything to make your holiday special.

parts.prompt: Your friends are planning a holiday and need somewhere to stay. Talk about these places and decide which one would be best.

parts.title: Talk about the topic
parts.instructions: Answer the questions. Try to give a reason or an example with each answer.

questions.prompt: What is the most important thing in a hotel room? Why?
Would you like to work in a hotel one day? Why or why not?
Do you think it is better to stay with friends or in a hotel?
